topic: value of the li; day's march
quote: he probably made his reckoning in days' journeys of 50 Li, or about ten English miles
finding: Lambrick takes 50 li as a day's march of about ten miles (5 li to the mile), allowing the li some elasticity with the terrain.

topic: value of the li; against Haig
quote: General Haig reckons a day's journev a' 100 Li…basil cbe pilgrim"• figures for biajoumeys whether loq or d.ort. io Sind
finding: He rejects Haig's 100 li a day (16 miles), preferring the shorter equivalent (1 li = 1½ furlongs) because on it the figures in Sind fit the geography.

topic: method: Records over Life; bearings to nearest cardinal point
quote: there seems no real difficulty in fixing the broad locations of the various regions he mentions if we follow his distances and his bearings
finding: He follows the Records' distances and bearings rather than the Life, allowing an elastic li and bearings rounded to the nearest cardinal point.

topic: route: Gurjara 1900 li N, crossing the Indus into Upper Sind
quote: It appears that Yuan Chwang came to S in d from the Gurjara…crossing the river…Sin-tu entered the kingdom of Sind
finding: He brings Xuanzang 1900 li north from Gurjara (Bhinmal), across the sands of Jaisalmer, to Upper Sind, crossing the Indus from its left to its right bank.

topic: country = kingdom of Sind incl. Salt Range and Derajat
quote: The mention of rock-salt indines us to suppose that this kingdom extended as far north as the Salt-range
finding: He identifies Sin-tu with the Rai kingdom of Sind of the Chachnama, reaching north to the Salt Range and over the Derajat; rock salt is his argument.

quote: It is generally assumed that the capital of Sind in 641-2 A .D. was at Alor
finding: He doubts the usual Alor: the pilgrim would have written A-lo-lo, and he reached the capital only after crossing the Indus, which then probably did not flow east of Alor.

topic: capital between Pano Akil and Kandhkot, right bank (eroded site)
quote: alluvial plain it may have bem eroded by the IDdus…oo the right bank of the ludus
finding: He suggests 毘苫婆補羅 (perhaps Vichavapura) stood in the alluvial plain between Pano Akil and Kandhkot on the right bank, later eroded by the Indus, the Rai then moving to Alor.

quote: His description of the organization of Sind in 642 A.O. as a metropolitan realm w1th dependent pro vinces
finding: He takes the metropolitan kingdom with dependent provinces as agreeing with the Chachnama's Sind under Rai Sahiras son of Sahasi.

quote: Among the low marshes near the…Sin-tu (Indus) for about 1000 Li were settled some myriads of
finding: He identifies Xuanzang's lawless herdsmen of the Indus marshes with the Jats (Luhana Jats) of the Chachnama.

quote: But this may be one…of the occasions, many of which occur in the text, when "cast"…appean by a copyist's mistake for "north east"
finding: He accepts Mou-lo-san-pu-lu = Multan from the sun temple with its golden image, against doubts on the transcription and bearing; it lay east of upper Sind (Derajat) or 'east' is a slip for north-east.

quote: observation that .Mou-lo-san-pu-lu, which may be identified…with Multan, was (in 642 A.O.) a dependency of the Che-ka
finding: He notes that Xuanzang makes Multan subject to Cheh-ka (Takka, capital near Sialkot), not Sind; Cheh-ka was probably the Chachnama's Takiah and temporarily independent of Sind.

quote: according to the "LifeH the pilgrim…proceeded from A-fan-t' u eastwJ.rd for 700 Li, which brought…him to the kingdom of Sind
finding: He records the Life's different order (A-fan-t'u 700 li E to Sind, then 900 li E across the Indus to Multan) but relies on the Records.

quote: He describes it as away in the west on the Indus and near the sea…This is evidently the h1dus Delta cowitry
finding: He identifies A-tien-p'o-chih-lo with the Indus Delta, reached 1500-1600 li south-west from Upper Sind.

quote: A-tien-p'o­…cbih-lo was thought by Cwmingham and Haig to be Cutch, and…its capital to be Koteshwar
finding: He rejects Cunningham's and Haig's Cutch and Koteshwar because the Chinese characters cannot render that name.

quote: the principal city of the…Delta country at this period. was known as Debal
finding: He takes the capital 朅䶩濕伐羅 (with its Maheśvara temple) to be Debal, 'temple' being a nickname for a city whose real name the pilgrim tried to render.

topic: country = Las Bela with Jhalawan and E Makran
quote: there can be…no doubt that it included the modem Las Bela, together probably…with parts of Jhalawan and Eastern Makran
finding: From 2000 li west of the Delta, the bay of the sea and subjection to Persia, he places Lang-kie-lo in Las Bela with parts of Jhalawan and eastern Makran; he names no capital site.

quote: He gives…the riame of the capital as Su-t'u-li-ssu-fa-lo, whidi Watters…renders as Stri-isvara
finding: He follows Watters' Stri-isvara and links the 'West Woman Country' with the Brihat Samhita's Stri-rajya and Nearchus' Woman's Harbour (Karachi).

quote: The explanation may be that the…pilgrim saw the…cowitry in a year of exceptionally favourable raiDfall
finding: He explains the reported fertility and population by a year of unusually good rain or by limited tracts such as the Welpat niabat of Las Bela.

topic: route: back to the Delta, then 700 li N, west of the Indus
quote: The pilgrim seems to have retraced his steps to the Delta…and thence to have proceeded northwards…for over 700 Li
finding: He has Xuanzang return from Lang-kie-lo to the Delta and go 700 li north without recrossing the Indus, so Pi-to-shih-lo lay west of the river.

quote: In fact this very argument…proves the exact contrary
finding: He rejects Cunningham's Patala/Hyderabad and Haig's Nagar Parkar or Umarkot: since no Indus crossing is mentioned, the country was west of the river, not east.

quote: We m a y therefore suppose that this regio n was round about…Sehwan, or possibly west of th\! Khirthar range, in Jhalawan
finding: He places Pi-to-shih-lo round Sehwan, preferring it to Jhalawan west of the Khirthar because nothing suggests mountains.

topic: country south of Larkana; capital Badah
quote: there seems fair ground…for believing that at Badah we haye the remains o f the capital of…this province
finding: 300 li north-east (read east of north) of Sehwan, A-fan-t'u lay south of Larkana with its capital at Badah; he cites Julien's 'O-fan-tcha (Avanda).

quote: may have been no other than the…Stupa at Mohen-jo-d.aro
finding: He suggests the Aśokan stupa north-east of the capital was the stupa at Mohenjo-daro, though he admits Mohenjo-daro lies east, not north-east, of the Buddhist settlement near Badah.

topic: country near Barkhan, not the Gomal
quote: I am inclined to think that Fa-la-na was…in the neighbourhood of Barkhan
finding: He places Fa-la-na near Barkhan, 900 li NE of A-fan-t'u, against the usual middle Gomal (Vaneh), which would make 900 li far too short and the 2000 li to Ghazni far too long.

topic: Gomal view based on the Life
quote: the pilgrim, during lhe early stages of bis return journey eo China
finding: He notes the Gomal view rests on the Life's 15 days south from Lan-po (Lamghan), but holds that his Barkhan site fits the Records' two stages along the hill routes.

topic: Ki-kiang-na = Kaikanan, in Loralai or Zhob
quote: we may suppose the tract…to have corresponded with Loralai or Zhob
finding: He identifies Ki-kiang-na with the Chachnama's Kaikanan, famous for horses and resistance to the Arabs, west of the Suleiman range, in Loralai or Zhob.

quote: the na me Kaikanan or Kaikan is…still a ttached to an ancient place much further to the so uth , near…Nal
finding: He sets aside the surviving Kaikan near Nal in Jhalawan as not fitting the itinerary, and cites Karkawan on Arab maps north of Kusdar opposite Multan.

quote: a cowitry…the capital of which evidently corresponds with Ghazni
finding: He takes the country 2000 li north-west of Fa-la-na to have its capital at Ghazni.

quote: Aauming that pilgrim started from the then capital of the Gurjara Statt'; Bbilmal
finding: He assumes the start from Bhinmal, about 300 miles north-west to the Indus in Upper Sind; the Life instead brings him into Lower Sind from Surashtra.

topic: Indus course in the 7th century: west of Alor
quote: which is not likely to have been· flowing east of Alor at that time
finding: He holds that in Xuanzang's time the Indus did not flow east of Alor; elsewhere he places it west of the Rohri hills, near the Lohano Dhoro, later deserting the Alor channel.

topic: Buddhism: Buddhist sites; Sind a Buddhist kingdom
quote: majorigy of these sites are distinguishable by Buddhist·· remains
finding: He counts about ten Buddhist sites in Central and Lower Sind and five in Upper Sind (Dhamrao near Badah, Mirpur Khas, Sudheran jo Daro), and calls Sind under the Rais 'the old Buddhist kingdom'.

finding: Following Cousens he takes the stupa at Depar Ghanghro as the Buddhist colony of Sawandi, perhaps the monastery of Budh Nohbahar visited by Rai Chach; he does not discuss Xuanzang's monastery counts or the Sammatiya.
